steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
summary: TACT-KV replaces standard full-precision or token/feature-statistics-based KV cache compression with a calibration-free separable 3D discrete cosine transform applied to the KV cache, followed by reverse-water-filling bit allocation across frequency bins and fixed-codebook scalar quantization. It costs an additional transform/inverse-transform step on KV states per layer (modest compute and implementation complexity) and introduces quantization distortion that is only bounded by spectral concentration of the cache; at aggressive 1-bit budgets some prediction flips still occur. It can fail when KV energy is not spatially concentrated along anatomical axes, when workloads lack 3D spatial structure, or when the method is applied to models or tasks whose accuracy is sensitive to low-bit frequency truncation, since gains were validated mainly on 3D medical imaging and video tasks.
rationale: The 8x batch-size claim at equal HBM is directly relevant to a single-GPU deployment, but the method targets 3D medical/video KV structure, so adoption should follow workload-specific validation on the reader's actual models and tasks.

claims.statement: TACT-KV replaces standard full-precision or token/feature-statistics-based KV cache compression with a calibration-free separable 3D discrete cosine transform applied to the KV cache, followed by reverse-water-filling bit allocation across frequency bins and fixed-codebook scalar quantization. It costs an additional transform/inverse-transform step on KV states per layer (modest compute and implementation complexity) and introduces quantization distortion that is only bounded by spectral concentration of the cache; at aggressive 1-bit budgets some prediction flips still occur. It can fail when KV energy is not spatially concentrated along anatomical axes, when workloads lack 3D spatial structure, or when the method is applied to models or tasks whose accuracy is sensitive to low-bit frequency truncation, since gains were validated mainly on 3D medical imaging and video tasks.

At equal HBM, TACT-KV scales decoding batch size on a single GPU by up to 8x, with the lowest 1-bit prediction-flip rate on 11 of 12 model-dataset pairs across six medical VLMs and two 3D CT benchmarks.
